title: Windows-style shortcuts + Linux Terminal + Windows modifiers in RDP (extended)

rules.description: [windows-karabiner] In Windows App, Option behaves as Windows key (safe version)
[windows-karabiner] Tap Option opens Launchpad on macOS — requires binding Cmd+Shift+L to Launchpad in System Settings → Keyboard → Shortcuts (not in Windows App, lazy tap/hold)
[windows-karabiner] In Windows App, Command behaves as Alt
[windows-karabiner] Option+D shows Desktop on macOS (Cmd+Shift+D — requires binding 'Show Desktop' to Cmd+Shift+D in System Settings → Keyboard → Shortcuts → Mission Control; not in Windows App)
[windows-karabiner] Option+Left/Right/Up tiles the focused window (sends Ctrl+Option+Arrow, matches macOS Tahoe built-in tiling and Rectangle defaults; not in Windows App)
[windows-karabiner] Windows-style Ctrl shortcuts for macOS apps (not Windows App / Terminal / iTerm2, with browser shortcuts)
[windows-karabiner] Windows-style Ctrl+Arrow/Delete navigation (not Windows App / Terminal / iTerm2)
[windows-karabiner] Windows-style Ctrl+Home/End jumps to document start/end (not Windows App / Terminal / iTerm2)
[windows-karabiner] Windows-style Home/End in normal apps (Cmd+Arrow, not Windows App / Terminal / iTerm2)
[windows-karabiner] Shell-style Home/End in Terminal and iTerm2 (Ctrl+A / Ctrl+E)
[windows-karabiner] Linux-style copy/paste in Terminal and iTerm2 (Ctrl+Shift+C/V)
[windows-karabiner] Windows-key-style shortcuts using Option (Finder, Spotlight, lock, minimize, close window; not Windows App)
[windows-karabiner] PrintScreen captures whole screen / Shift+PrintScreen captures region (not Windows App)
[windows-karabiner] F2 in Finder renames the selected item (Windows-style rename)
